text:
The Denver Gazette's Evan Rawal made the case this week that Devon Toews has been Colorado's best player, and it's hard to argue. He has 18 points in 19 games, after 24 in 68 last season, and the Avalanche take 60% of the expected goals at five on five with him on, the best share on the team.

Our numbers call the hot streak earned: he's getting more chances of his own, not just riding his partner's. But there's a lot of luck mixed in. Colorado has scored 11.3 more goals than expected with him on the ice, and he's shooting 17% after 3% last season. His points per 60 are double the top of our range for him. Something has to give.

What won't give is the player underneath. Evolving-Hockey had him in the 94th percentile among defensemen for driving offense last season, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has him in the 96th percentile for setups. Our range: 40 to 59 points.
